# gloci — Agent Usage Guide

<!-- Generated by: cargo xtask docs --skill SKILL.md -->

## Core semantics

- **0-based half-open coordinates:** Internally every feature is a 0-based, half-open interval `[start, end)` with 64-bit unsigned coordinates (BED is 0-based `[start, end)`; GFF/GTF is 1-based closed `[start, end]`; VCF/BCF is 1-based `POS`; CLI `--region` strings are 1-based inclusive `chr1:1,000-2,000`). Input format is auto-detected from content, never extensions (`--format`, `--a-format`, `--b-format` override; `-` reads stdin; `.gz` output is always BGZF; `-o FILE` writes atomically).
- **Points and overlap:** Zero-length features (`start == end`, e.g. BED insertion sites or pure VCF insertions) are points between bases. Non-empty intervals overlap when they share a base (`max(a.start, b.start) < min(a.end, b.end)`). A point overlaps an interval only when strictly inside it (`start < p < end`), or on either edge with `--inclusive-points`; two points overlap when equal. Every overlap threshold (`-f`, `-F`, `-r`, `-e`, `--min-bases`) counts as met when either side is a point.
- **VCF allele footprints:** By default (`--vcf-span allele`), a VCF/BCF record spans the reference bases its ALT alleles change after trimming shared REF/ALT prefixes and suffixes (a pure insertion is a point at `POS`; a deletion excludes its anchor base; multi-allelic records span the union of ALT footprints). Pass `--vcf-span ref` for `[POS-1, POS-1+len(REF))` (reproducing bedtools, tabix, and bcftools).
- **Karyotype vs lexicographic chromosome order:** Chromosome order priority is `-g` (built-in genome such as `hg38` or `GRCh38`, or `.fai`/`.genome`/`.dict`/BAM/VCF header) > first VCF/BCF header's `##contig` lines > `--chrom-order` (default `karyotype`: `chr1, chr2 ... chr22, chrX, chrY, chrM`; `--chrom-order lex` gives byte order `chr1, chr10 ... chr2`).
- **Sortedness errors and fixes:** Streaming commands (`intersect`, `subtract`, `closest`, `map`, `coverage`, `merge`, `complement`) verify `(chrom, start)` order on the fly and exit 1 on the first violation. Fix unsorted or lex-sorted inputs with one of:
  - `--sort`: externally sorts inputs first bounded by `--max-mem` (spilling to `--tmp-dir`).
  - `--unsorted` (`intersect`, `subtract`, `closest`, `map`, `coverage`): loads all `-b` files into memory and streams `-a` in its original order.
  - `--chrom-order lex`: accepts and preserves lexicographic chromosome order (from `bedtools sort`, `sort-bed`, or `LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1`).
- **VCF passthrough vs TSV output:** Commands that emit A's records unchanged (`view`, `sort`, `intersect --mode any|none`, `subtract`, `vcf filter`) write A's format (VCF A keeps its header plus a `##glociCommand` line). Commands that append columns (`intersect --mode pairs|count`, `closest`, `map`, `coverage`) write TSV (VCF A gets a single `#CHROM\tPOS...` column-name line and no meta-header; BED/GFF A keep headers only with `--header`). `merge`, `complement`, `windows`, and `convert` write BED.

## Command reference

### `gloci genomes`

List the built-in genomes that -g accepts, or print one.

Without a subcommand, prints one line per built-in genome with the columns id, species, assembly, naming (ucsc or ensembl), sequences and total_bp, separated by tabs. The lengths come from UCSC chrom.sizes files and from the Ensembl core databases; the sources are recorded in data/genomes/SOURCES.toml in the source tree.

```sh
gloci genomes
gloci genomes show hg38
gloci sort peaks.bed -g hg38 > peaks.sorted.bed
```

#### `gloci genomes show`

Print one built-in genome as name and length, tab-separated.

The chromosomes come in the order -g uses for sorting. The output is a valid .genome file, so it can also be saved and edited.

```sh
gloci genomes show hg38
gloci genomes show GRCh38 > GRCh38.genome
gloci genomes show mm39 | cut -f1
```

### `gloci index`

Build a .tbi/.csi index for a sorted BGZF file.

BED, GFF/GTF, VCF and BCF files are recognised by content. Any other tab-separated file is indexed like tabix does when you name its columns with -s (sequence), -b (begin) and -e (end, optional). The columns are numbered from 1. Without --zero-based the begin column is 1-based and a feature covers [begin-1, end]; with it, [begin, end). Without -e a feature covers one base. Lines starting with --comment (default #) and the first --skip-lines lines are not indexed; both are recorded in the index. Chromosomes must be contiguous and sorted by begin. The index is a .tbi, or a .csi when an end passes 2^29.

```sh
gloci index calls.vcf.gz
gloci index peaks.bed.gz -t 8
gloci index scores.tsv.gz -s 1 -b 2 -e 3 --zero-based
gloci index sites.txt.gz -s 1 -b 2 --skip-lines 1 --comment %
```

### `gloci sort`

Sort BED/bedGraph/GFF/VCF/BCF files with bounded memory.

Records are ordered by chromosome, then start, then end. The chromosome order comes from -g, else from the ##contig lines of a VCF/BCF header, else from --chrom-order (karyotype by default). Records that tie keep their input order unless --full-key is given. BED header lines are kept only with --header; the leading ## lines of a GFF and the header of a VCF/BCF are always kept. VCF/BCF records are ordered by POS and REF end whatever --vcf-span says, so the output is tabix-compatible. The output format is the input format: -o must match it. Use -o with the same path as an input to sort a file in place.

Sorting spills to --tmp-dir when the input is larger than --max-mem. That directory must exist and be writable; it is checked before any input is read.

```sh
gloci sort peaks.bed > peaks.sorted.bed
gloci sort calls.vcf.gz -o calls.sorted.vcf.gz --write-index
gloci sort huge.bed --max-mem 8G --tmp-dir /scratch -t 16 -o huge.sorted.bed.gz
gloci sort --check peaks.sorted.bed
```

### `gloci view`

Print the records in regions, stream or recompress a file, convert VCF to BCF and back, or print only the header.

With no regions the records are written as read (comment and track lines after the first record and blank lines are dropped, and CRLF line ends become LF), so view can recompress a file (-o FILE.gz is BGZF) or index it (--write-index). VCF and BCF convert to each other with -O or the -o extension; the header is kept as it is, plus a ##glociCommand line. BED and GFF header lines are kept by default. For conversions to BED from VCF/BCF, GFF3/GTF or BED12, use gloci convert.

With regions, view prints the records whose footprint (per --vcf-span) overlaps a region, each once, in file order. A point (a zero-length BED record, an insertion) overlaps a region only when strictly inside it, unless --inclusive-points is given. Regions are read through a .tbi/.csi index when the file has one, and otherwise by scanning the whole file, with a warning. Either way the order of every record read is checked, so an unsorted file is an error, never a wrong answer. With --assume-sorted, an uncompressed BED file without an index is binary-searched instead (like bedextract); that trusts the file to be sorted. Index the file (gloci sort FILE -o FILE.gz --write-index) for speed and checking both.

```sh
gloci view calls.vcf.gz chr1:1,000,000-2,000,000 chrX
gloci view peaks.bed --regions-file targets.bed --inclusive-points
gloci view calls.bcf -O vcf | less
gloci view calls.vcf.gz -o calls.bcf --write-index
```

### `gloci check`

Validate files and print a one-screen summary of each.

check reads every file to the end, keeps going past problems and reports the record count, the chromosomes, whether the records are sorted, and the first 10 errors and warnings with their line numbers. Errors: records that do not parse, records out of order, an end past the chromosome length or a chromosome missing from -g, bad BED12 blocks, a bedGraph value that is not a number, a VCF line with the wrong number of columns. Warnings: exact duplicate lines at the same position, and blank lines. Exit status 1 when any file has errors. The order is checked against -g, else the ##contig lines of a VCF/BCF, else --chrom-order (karyotype by default).

```sh
gloci check peaks.bed
gloci check calls.vcf.gz -g hg38.fa.fai
gloci check a.bed b.bed --chrom-order lex
```

### `gloci intersect`

Report the records of A that overlap, or do not overlap, records of B.

The default mode is any: A's records that overlap at least one B record are written as read, in A's format. --mode picks another report: none (A's records with no overlap), pairs (one TSV row per overlapping A and B pair; --overlap-bases adds the shared bases and --keep-unmatched adds a row with placeholder B columns for each A without one), clip (A cut to the shared span, once per overlap) and count (A with its number of overlaps, summed over all -b files). With several -b files, pairs rows carry a label column (--names, else the file basename) before B's columns; unmatched rows get `.`.

Overlap follows spec section 4.3: records overlap when they share a base, a point overlaps an interval when strictly inside it (or on its edge with --inclusive-points), and every threshold (-f, -F, -r, -e, --min-bases) is met when either side is a point. Thresholds are measured against B's own span; they cannot be combined with -w, --left or --right. A VCF/BCF record covers the bases its ALT alleles change (--vcf-span). --match alleles also requires some ALT of A to equal some ALT of B after trimming (VCF/BCF inputs only).

A and every B must be sorted in one chromosome order, which is checked as they are read; a violation is an error with a fix. With --unsorted, any order works, A is still streamed and reported in its own order, and every -b file is loaded into memory, so memory grows with the size of B. Pairs and count write TSV (a VCF A gets a #CHROM line naming the columns); clip does not accept VCF/BCF.

Two ways to deal with inputs that are not sorted. Use --sort when the inputs are too big for memory or you want sorted output: A and every -b file are sorted first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem (spilling to --tmp-dir), then the normal sweep runs, so the result equals gloci sort on each input followed by this command. It needs disk, about twice the input size in --tmp-dir, and removes it afterwards. Use --unsorted when you want A's order kept and every -b file fits in memory. The two cannot be combined.

When A and every -b file are BGZF files with a .tbi or .csi index and more than one thread is used, the work runs on runs of chromosomes in parallel, which are read and written in the chromosome-table order (karyotype by default; -g, a VCF header or --chrom-order set it). At most 8 runs are in flight (more threads speed up BGZF); their output waiting to be written shares 64 MiB of memory and the rest spills to --tmp-dir. Indexed and streaming runs give identical output for inputs in chromosome-table order; an input that is not in table order is refused with the same error whatever the thread count.

```sh
gloci intersect -a peaks.bed -b genes.bed
gloci intersect -a calls.vcf.gz -b exons.bed --mode none -o off_target.vcf.gz
gloci intersect -a a.bed -b x.bed y.bed --mode pairs --overlap-bases --names X,Y
gloci intersect -a reads.bed -b targets.bed -f 50% -s --mode count --unsorted
```

### `gloci merge`

Merge overlapping or nearby records into clusters (bedtools merge, bedops -m).

Records are grouped by their footprints: a record joins the open cluster when its start is at most the cluster end plus -d/--max-gap. The default 0 joins overlapping and bookended features; a negative gap such as -d -2 needs at least that many shared bases; a point joins a cluster it lies inside or touches. The output is BED (chrom, start, end), or TSV for -o x.tsv, and is not A's records. --count adds the number of records per cluster and -c COL:OP adds one aggregation column per option (count, sum, mean, median, min, max, stdev, var, stdev_pop, var_pop, collapse, distinct, distinct_sorted, first, last, count_distinct, indicator, cv, mad, quantile:Q, tmean:LO-HI, mode, antimode; the ops that need a second input, like wmean, are for map). -s clusters each strand separately (unknown strand apart from + and -) without adding a strand column.

Several files are merged together as one stream. Every input must be sorted in one chromosome order, which is checked as it is read; an unsorted input is an error whose hint is to run gloci sort or to pass --sort, which sorts the inputs first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem (spilling to --tmp-dir); the result equals gloci sort FILES | gloci merge -. Memory stays flat apart from the clusters being built.

```sh
gloci merge peaks.bed
gloci merge a.bed b.bed -d 100 --count
gloci merge genes.bed -s -c 5:max -c 4:distinct
gloci merge calls.vcf.gz -d -1 -o regions.bed.gz --write-index
```

### `gloci cluster`

Give every record the id of its cluster (bedtools cluster).

Writes each input line unchanged followed by a tab and a cluster id. Clusters are those of gloci merge, with the same -d/--max-gap (default 0: overlapping and bookended records share a cluster; a negative gap needs that many shared bases) and -s (each strand clustered separately, unknown strand apart from + and -). Ids start at 1 and increase through the file, across chromosomes. With -s, a cluster takes the next id when its first record is read, and the records stay in input order (bedtools cluster -s regroups them by strand within each chromosome).

The output is TSV, not a copy of the input format: a VCF input (clustered by its footprints, see --vcf-span) gets a #CHROM column line ending in "cluster" and then its records with the id appended. --header keeps the header lines of a BED or GFF input. The input must be sorted in one chromosome order, checked as it is read; pass --sort to sort it first.

```sh
gloci cluster peaks.bed
gloci cluster peaks.bed -d 100 -s
gloci cluster calls.vcf.gz --vcf-span ref -d 50
```

### `gloci spacing`

Give every record its distance to the previous record (bedtools spacing).

Writes each input line unchanged followed by a tab and the number of bases between the record and the one before it in the file on the same chromosome: . for the first record of a chromosome, 0 when they are bookended, -1 when their footprints overlap (including a record inside the previous one; only the previous record counts). Unlike bedtools, a zero-length record is a point on its base rather than a base wide on each side. The output is TSV, not a copy of the input format; for VCF input see gloci cluster. The input must be sorted in one chromosome order; pass --sort to sort it first.

```sh
gloci spacing peaks.bed
gloci spacing calls.vcf.gz --vcf-span ref
```

### `gloci complement`

Write the bases no feature covers (bedtools complement, bedops -c).

Features of all files are united, and the gaps between them are written as BED (chrom, start, end). With -g, the gaps are taken over each chromosome of the genome, in genome order: a chromosome with no features becomes one row over its whole length, and the gaps before the first and after the last feature are included. The genome needs lengths (a built-in genome, .genome, .fai or .dict file); a feature that reaches past the end of its chromosome is an error. Without -g only the gaps between features of the same chromosome are written. Points cover no bases and are ignored. Bookended features leave no gap.

Every input must be sorted in one chromosome order, which is checked as it is read; with -g, use the genome's own order (gloci sort -g). An unsorted input is an error whose hint names --sort, which sorts the inputs first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem; the result equals gloci sort FILES | gloci complement -.

```sh
gloci complement peaks.bed
gloci complement peaks.bed -g hg38 -o uncovered.bed
gloci complement a.bed b.bed -g sacCer3
gloci complement shuffled.bed -g genome.txt --sort --max-mem 512M
```

### `gloci partition`

Split the inputs at every boundary into segments and say who covers each (bedtools multiinter and unionbedg, bedops -p, -i and -s).

The footprints of all files are cut at every start and end, giving disjoint segments in sorted order. Each row is chrom, start, end, the number of files covering the segment and their labels joined with commas (--names, default the file names without directories). A file counts once however many of its features overlap there, and points cover no bases, so they add neither segments nor boundaries. Only segments covered by at least one file are written. --min-files K and --max-files K keep segments covered by at least or at most K files; --all keeps those covered by every file. --empty implies --min-files 0 (an explicit --min-files overrides it); --min-files 0 needs --empty. By default a boundary is kept even where the membership does not change (as in bedops -p); --merge-adjacent joins neighbouring segments with the same output columns (as multiinter does). --no-membership writes coordinates only, so with --merge-adjacent every run of touching kept segments is joined.

With --bedgraph the inputs are bedGraph files and each row has one value per file instead of the membership; a file that does not cover the segment shows --empty (default 0). Giving --empty also writes the segments no file covers, with that value in every column; with -g (needs lengths) it covers whole chromosomes, including those with no features, otherwise only the gaps between features. The intervals of one bedGraph must not overlap.

Every input must be sorted in one chromosome order, which is checked as it is read; an unsorted input is an error whose hint names --sort, which sorts each file first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem. Memory is bounded by the intervals open at one position.

```sh
gloci partition a.bed b.bed c.bed --merge-adjacent
gloci partition a.bed b.bed --names tumour,normal --min-files 2
gloci partition a.bed b.bed --all --merge-adjacent --no-membership
gloci partition a.bg b.bg --bedgraph --empty 0 -g hg38
```

### `gloci genomecov`

Depth of coverage of a genome by the features of a BED file (bedtools genomecov -i).

Every feature adds one to the depth over its bases. -g is required: the output covers every chromosome of the genome from base 0 to its length, in genome order, chromosomes without features included (a built-in genome, .genome, .fai or .dict file with lengths). The default --hist writes, per chromosome and then for the whole genome (chrom `genome`), one row per depth present: chrom, depth, bases at that depth, chromosome length, fraction (six significant digits, as bedtools). --bedgraph writes runs of equal depth above zero, --bga also the zero-depth runs, --per-base one row per base: chrom, 1-based position, depth. --scale X multiplies the depths of the last three (six significant digits, as bedtools); --max-depth N puts every depth of N or more into the bin N of --hist. --strand + or - counts only features on that strand (BED needs column 6; a feature with unknown strand is not counted). --split counts the BED12 blocks of each feature. --5p and --3p count one base per feature, its 5' or 3' end by strand (unknown counts as plus). A zero-length feature covers no bases and is ignored. A feature past the end of its chromosome is an error. BAM input is not supported yet.

The input must be sorted in the genome order, which is checked as it is read; an unsorted input is an error whose hint names --sort. Memory is bounded by the features open at one position, whatever the output mode.

```sh
gloci genomecov peaks.bed -g hg38
gloci genomecov reads.bed -g hg38 --bedgraph --scale 0.000001 -o cov.bedgraph
gloci genomecov genes.bed -g genome.txt --bga --strand +
gloci genomecov exons12.bed -g hg38 --split --per-base
```

### `gloci slop`

Grow each feature on its sides (bedtools slop, bedops --range).

Every record is written with its coordinates changed to [start - L, end + R), clipped at 0 and, with -g, at the end of its chromosome (a built-in genome, .genome, .fai or .dict file with lengths; a chromosome missing from it is an error). Amounts are bases, or with --pct a decimal fraction of each feature's length (0.5 or 50%, floored). -b pads both sides; --left and --right pad one each. -s swaps them for minus-strand records (an unknown strand counts as plus). BED and GFF/GTF only; VCF/BCF input is a usage error. The input is streamed in its own order and needs no sorting; the output keeps the input format, and a warning is printed once when -s or --pct makes it go out of order.

```sh
gloci slop genes.bed -b 1000 -g hg38
gloci slop genes.bed --left 2000 --right 500 -s -g hg38 -o promoters.bed
gloci slop peaks.bed --pct -b 0.5 -g genome.txt
gloci slop annotation.gff3 -b 100 -g hg38
```

### `gloci flank`

Write the strips beside each feature (bedtools flank).

For every record, a left strip [start - L, start) and then a right strip [end, end + R) are written as records with the input's other columns, clipped at 0 and, with -g, at the chromosome end. A strip clipped to nothing is not written. Options as for slop: -b, --left, --right, -s, --pct, -g. The output is in input order and may not be sorted; a warning is printed once when it goes out of order.

```sh
gloci flank genes.bed -b 100 -g hg38
gloci flank genes.bed --left 2000 -s -g hg38
gloci flank peaks.bed --pct -b 0.25 -g genome.txt | gloci sort -g genome.txt -
```

### `gloci shift`

Move each feature along its chromosome (bedtools shift).

--by N moves every record by N bases (negative moves toward 0); --pct reads N as a fraction of the feature's own length (0.5, -25%; the product is floored using exact decimal arithmetic). -s negates the shift on minus-strand records (an unknown strand counts as +), so a positive N moves every feature downstream. The result is clipped like slop: at 0 and, with -g, at the chromosome end, so a feature pushed over an edge shrinks; one pushed wholly over an edge becomes the 1-base interval at that edge, as in bedtools (a zero-length feature stays zero-length there). BED and GFF/GTF only. The output is in input order and may not be sorted; a warning is printed once when the shift itself breaks the order.

```sh
gloci shift genes.bed --by 100 -g hg38
gloci shift genes.bed --by -50 -g hg38
gloci shift peaks.bed --by 1000 -s -g hg38 | gloci sort -g hg38 -
gloci shift peaks.bed --pct --by 0.5 -g genome.txt
```

### `gloci windows`

Cut chromosomes or intervals into windows (bedtools makewindows, bedops --chop).

-g cuts every chromosome of a genome (built-in, .genome, .fai or .dict with lengths) in genome order; -i cuts the footprint of every record of a file in input order (no sorting needed; points give no windows; -i - reads stdin). -w SIZE gives windows of SIZE bases every --step bases (default SIZE; a smaller step overlaps, a larger one leaves gaps), the last one truncated at the interval end. -n COUNT gives COUNT windows of floor(length / COUNT) bases, the last one taking the remainder; an interval shorter than COUNT is skipped with a warning. Output is BED3; --id-column adds the 1-based window number of each source interval, counted from the end with --reverse.

```sh
gloci windows -g hg38 -w 1000000 -o bins.bed
gloci windows -g genome.txt -w 1000 --step 500
gloci windows -i genes.bed -n 10 --id-column --reverse
gloci merge peaks.bed | gloci windows -i - -w 100
```

### `gloci convert`

Convert VCF/BCF, GFF3/GTF, WIG or BED12 to BED (bedops convert2bed, vcf2bed, gff2bed, gtf2bed; bedtools bed12tobed6).

VCF/BCF gives one row per record: chrom, start, end, ID, REF, ALT, QUAL, FILTER, with the footprint chosen by --vcf-span. --split-alleles writes one row per ALT instead, each with that ALT's own footprint (with --vcf-span ref, the record's REF footprint on every row; `*`, `<*>` and `<NON_REF>` rows are skipped when other ALTs exist). --types keeps the records (with --split-alleles, the ALTs) of the listed kinds: snv, mnv, ins, del, sv, ref, other; a record is kept when any of its ALTs is of a listed kind. GFF3/GTF gives 10 columns (bedops gff2bed): chrom, start, end, name, score, strand, source, type, phase, attributes. The name is the --name-attr attribute (default ID for GFF3, gene_id for GTF; `.` when absent). --feature keeps the listed column-3 types. WIG (fixedStep or variableStep, with optional span) gives one bedGraph row per data line: chrom, start, end, value; equal values are not merged. fixedStep needs start= and step=; values must be finite. A span larger than the step gives overlapping rows. BED12 with --blocks gives one BED6 row per block; a line that is not valid BED12 (fewer than 12 columns, block counts that disagree, blocks out of order, a last block not ending at chromEnd) is an error, also with --skip-invalid. The input is converted in its own order and needs no sorting. A conversion whose output goes out of order (allele footprints can start after their record) prints one warning; --write-index then fails.

```sh
gloci convert calls.vcf.gz -o calls.bed
gloci convert calls.vcf.gz --split-alleles --types del,ins
gloci convert genes.gtf --feature exon --name-attr gene_name
gloci convert transcripts.bed --blocks -o exons.bed
```

### `gloci subtract`

Remove from A the bases covered by B (bedtools subtract, bedops -d).

Each A record is cut by the union of the B records that overlap it, and what is left is written as A's own record with new coordinates: one record per piece, in ascending order (BED columns 2-3, GFF columns 4-5). An A that nothing touches is written as read, and an A that is covered completely disappears. A point has no bases to cut: it is dropped when a B contains it, and a B point removes nothing from a cut; under --whole, or --sum-overlaps without -f, a B point strictly inside A (or on its edge with --inclusive-points) still removes A (the point rule of intersect). The criteria (-f, -F, -r, -e, --min-bases, -s, -S) choose which B count and are measured as in intersect. -w, --left and --right pad B before it cuts.

--whole drops an A that has any counting B instead of cutting it (bedtools -A). --sum-overlaps drops an A when the bases shared with all the B that pass the strand rule add up to at least -f of A (bedtools -N); it takes only -f, and without -f it acts like --whole. --split cuts by the BED12 blocks of B, not its span. A VCF/BCF A is never cut: a record is dropped whole, in default or --whole mode when intersect --mode none would drop it (any accepted hit), or with --sum-overlaps -f when the summed overlaps reach -f of its footprint, and the output is VCF with its header.

A and every B must be sorted in one chromosome order, which is checked as they are read. With --unsorted, any order works, A is still streamed and written in its own order, and every -b file is loaded into memory, so memory grows with the size of B.

Two ways to deal with inputs that are not sorted. Use --sort when the inputs are too big for memory or you want sorted output: A and every -b file are sorted first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem (spilling to --tmp-dir), then the normal sweep runs, so the result equals gloci sort on each input followed by this command. It needs disk, about twice the input size in --tmp-dir, and removes it afterwards. Use --unsorted when you want A's order kept and every -b file fits in memory. The two cannot be combined.

When A and every -b file are BGZF files with a .tbi or .csi index and more than one thread is used, the work runs on runs of chromosomes in parallel, which are read and written in the chromosome-table order (karyotype by default; -g, a VCF header or --chrom-order set it). At most 8 runs are in flight (more threads speed up BGZF); their output waiting to be written shares 64 MiB of memory and the rest spills to --tmp-dir. Indexed and streaming runs give identical output for inputs in chromosome-table order; an input that is not in table order is refused with the same error whatever the thread count.

```sh
gloci subtract -a peaks.bed -b blacklist.bed
gloci subtract -a genes.bed -b repeats.bed -f 50% --whole -o clean.bed
gloci subtract -a reads.bed -b exons.bed --sum-overlaps -f 0.8 -s
gloci subtract -a calls.vcf.gz -b blacklist.bed -o filtered.vcf.gz
```

### `gloci closest`

Find the nearest B to each A (bedtools closest, bedops closest-features).

For each A, reports the nearest B as TSV rows: A's record, a label column when there are several -b files, B's record, and with --distance the distance. An overlapping B has distance 0, bookended features 1, and otherwise the gap in bases plus 1. An A with no candidate gets one row with a placeholder B (`. -1 -1 ...`) and distance -1. A VCF/BCF A gets a column-name line.

-k N reports the N nearest, and every B tied with the N-th. With --ties first or last, only as many of the tied B as N still needs are kept: the first or the last by (file, input order). Rows are ordered by distance, then by file and input order. --signed ref|a|b prints signed distances (and implies --distance): negative is upstream, where ref means lower coordinates, a follows A's strand and b follows B's strand; unknown strand counts as +. --ignore-upstream and --ignore-downstream drop B by that sign in the same frame (ref when --signed is absent), --ignore-overlaps drops overlapping B, and --max-distance N drops B farther than N. -s and -S keep only B on the same or the opposite strand; B and A of unknown strand never match.

--each-side writes one row per A with the nearest upstream B and then the nearest downstream B; with --distance each distance is signed (as closest-features does). An overlapping B counts on both sides. -k applies per side, and extra ranks and ties add rows. With several -b files, the nearest are chosen across all of them, or with --per-file in each file, whose rows are written in file order; a file with no candidate for an A writes no row (as bedtools -mdb each), and an A with no candidate in any file gets one placeholder row. --each-side with --ignore-upstream or --ignore-downstream leaves that side empty except for an overlapping B, which still shows there at distance 0 unless --ignore-overlaps is given.

Memory and a pathology: the sorted sweep looks ahead in B for the nearest B to the right of A. Under -s/-S, or with --signed b and --ignore-upstream, --ignore-downstream or --each-side, a chromosome where one strand has no B left makes the look-ahead read and buffer all the remaining B of that chromosome. --max-distance bounds this. With --unsorted every -b file is loaded into memory instead, so memory grows with the size of B, and A is streamed and written in its own order.

Two ways to deal with inputs that are not sorted. Use --sort when the inputs are too big for memory or you want sorted output: A and every -b file are sorted first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem (spilling to --tmp-dir), then the normal sweep runs, so the result equals gloci sort on each input followed by this command. It needs disk, about twice the input size in --tmp-dir, and removes it afterwards. Use --unsorted when you want A's order kept and every -b file fits in memory. The two cannot be combined.

When A and every -b file are BGZF files with a .tbi or .csi index and more than one thread is used, the work runs on runs of chromosomes in parallel, which are read and written in the chromosome-table order (karyotype by default; -g, a VCF header or --chrom-order set it). At most 8 runs are in flight (more threads speed up BGZF); their output waiting to be written shares 64 MiB of memory and the rest spills to --tmp-dir. Indexed and streaming runs give identical output for inputs in chromosome-table order; an input that is not in table order is refused with the same error whatever the thread count.

```sh
gloci closest -a genes.bed -b peaks.bed --distance
gloci closest -a genes.bed -b peaks.bed -k 3 --signed a -s
gloci closest -a snps.vcf.gz -b genes.bed --max-distance 10000 --ignore-overlaps
gloci closest -a genes.bed -b peaks.bed --each-side --distance
```

### `gloci map`

Aggregate columns of the B records over each A (bedtools map, bedops bedmap).

For each A, in A's order, folds the B records that overlap it (the criteria of intersect: -f, -F, -r, -e, --min-bases, -s, -S, --split, or a window -w/--left/--right) and writes A's record followed by one column per -c COL:OP, in B file then B input order. COL is a 1-based column of B, 0 for the whole record (count, bases, indicator, bases_uniq, frac_a, frac_b and records only), or for a VCF B QUAL, ID, FILTER or INFO/KEY. Ops: count count_distinct sum mean median min max stdev var stdev_pop var_pop collapse distinct distinct_sorted first last bases indicator cv mad quantile:Q tmean:LO-HI wmean mode antimode bases_uniq frac_a frac_b min_record max_record records (COL 0 also works with bases_uniq, frac_a, frac_b and records; records ignores COL). cv is the sample stdev over the mean; mad the unscaled median absolute deviation; quantile is type 7 and tmean the mean of the values whose rank fraction is within LO-HI (a lone value is kept); wmean weights by overlapping bases; ties of mode and antimode go to the bytewise smallest value, as in bedtools; bases_uniq counts overlapped bases once; frac_a is bases_uniq over A's length and frac_b the summed overlap over the summed B length (--empty when the length is 0); records copies whole B records, tabs shown as |, and does not escape --delim where it occurs in the data. count counts every overlapping B; the other ops skip `.` and empty values, and a value that is not a number in a numeric op is an error. sum, min and max print integers when every value was one; stdev and var are sample statistics (one value gives --empty); stdev_pop and var_pop divide by n (one value gives 0), as bedtools stdev does. bases is the overlap of A with each B's own span, which is 0 for a B that is within a window only; indicator is 1 when any B counts, else 0. An A with no B gets 0 for count and count_distinct and --empty (default `.`) for the rest; --skip-unmatched drops such A instead.

Columns are resolved against the first -b file, and all -b files must be one format family. The output is TSV with A's columns first; a VCF/BCF A gets a column-name line ending with the -c labels.

A and every B must be sorted in one chromosome order, which is checked as they are read. With --unsorted, any order works, A is still streamed in its own order, and every -b file is loaded into memory, so memory grows with the size of B.

Two ways to deal with inputs that are not sorted. Use --sort when the inputs are too big for memory or you want sorted output: A and every -b file are sorted first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem (spilling to --tmp-dir), then the normal sweep runs, so the result equals gloci sort on each input followed by this command. It needs disk, about twice the input size in --tmp-dir, and removes it afterwards. Use --unsorted when you want A's order kept and every -b file fits in memory. The two cannot be combined.

When A and every -b file are BGZF files with a .tbi or .csi index and more than one thread is used, the work runs on runs of chromosomes in parallel, which are read and written in the chromosome-table order (karyotype by default; -g, a VCF header or --chrom-order set it). At most 8 runs are in flight (more threads speed up BGZF); their output waiting to be written shares 64 MiB of memory and the rest spills to --tmp-dir. Indexed and streaming runs give identical output for inputs in chromosome-table order; an input that is not in table order is refused with the same error whatever the thread count.

```sh
gloci map -a genes.bed -b scores.bedgraph -c 4:mean
gloci map -a windows.bed -b peaks.bed -c 0:count -c 5:max --skip-unmatched
gloci map -a snps.vcf.gz -b regions.bed -c 4:distinct --delim ';'
gloci map -a genes.bed -b peaks.bed -w 100 -c 0:count -c 0:bases
```

### `gloci coverage`

How much of each A the B records cover (bedtools coverage and annotate).

For each A, in A's order, counts the B records that overlap it (the criteria of intersect: -f, -F, -r, -e, --min-bases, -s, -S, --split, --inclusive-points) and writes A's record followed by the number of hits, the bases of A covered by at least one hit, A's length and the covered fraction. --hist writes one row per depth present in A (depth, bases at that depth, A's length, fraction) and, after the last A, `all` rows with the totals. --per-base writes one row per base of A (1-based offset, depth). --mean writes the mean depth over A. With several -b files only the default report is allowed and each file gives one covered fraction (bedtools annotate).

With --split, A and B are their BED12 blocks: depth counts the bases shared by an A block and a B block, A's length is the sum of its blocks, and --per-base offsets run along the blocks. A point A covers no bases: it reports its hit count, 0, 0 and `.`, --mean gives `.`, and --hist and --per-base write no rows for it. Fractions and means print in the shortest exact decimal form (0.3, not 0.3000000).

A and every B must be sorted in one chromosome order, which is checked as they are read. With --unsorted, any order works, A is still streamed in its own order, and every -b file is loaded into memory, so memory grows with the size of B. The output is TSV with A's columns first.

Two ways to deal with inputs that are not sorted. Use --sort when the inputs are too big for memory or you want sorted output: A and every -b file are sorted first with an external sort bounded by --max-mem (spilling to --tmp-dir), then the normal sweep runs, so the result equals gloci sort on each input followed by this command. It needs disk, about twice the input size in --tmp-dir, and removes it afterwards. Use --unsorted when you want A's order kept and every -b file fits in memory. The two cannot be combined.

When A and every -b file are BGZF files with a .tbi or .csi index and more than one thread is used, the work runs on runs of chromosomes in parallel, which are read and written in the chromosome-table order (karyotype by default; -g, a VCF header or --chrom-order set it). At most 8 runs are in flight (more threads speed up BGZF); their output waiting to be written shares 64 MiB of memory and the rest spills to --tmp-dir. Indexed and streaming runs give identical output for inputs in chromosome-table order; an input that is not in table order is refused with the same error whatever the thread count.

```sh
gloci coverage -a genes.bed -b reads.bed
gloci coverage -a genes.bed -b reads.bed --hist
gloci coverage -a exons.bed -b reads.bed --per-base -s
gloci coverage -a peaks.bed -b rep1.bed rep2.bed --names r1,r2
```

### `gloci groupby`

Aggregate columns over runs of lines with equal keys (bedtools groupby).

Reads any tab-separated text, BED included, and groups consecutive lines whose -g key columns are equal; the input does not have to be sorted, and a key that comes back later starts a new group (as in bedtools groupby; sort first to get one group per key). Each group writes its key columns, exactly as in its first line, followed by one column per -c COL:OP, with the ops of map (count, count_distinct, sum, mean, median, min, max, stdev, var, stdev_pop, var_pop, collapse, distinct, distinct_sorted, first, last, indicator, cv, mad, quantile:Q, tmean:LO-HI, mode, antimode); the ops that need a second input (wmean, records, min_record, max_record, frac_*, bases_uniq, bases) are for map. Blank lines, `#` lines and track/browser lines are skipped. A line with fewer columns than -g needs is an error naming the line.

With --header the first line names the columns: -g and -c may use the names, and the output starts with a line holding the key names and the -c labels (bedtools -header copies the input header unchanged). VCF and BCF input is refused; extract the fields first with gloci vcf extract. --threads is accepted for uniformity with the other commands; groupby runs on a single thread.

```sh
gloci groupby scores.bed -g 1,2 -c 5:sum -c 5:mean
gloci groupby calls.tsv -g 1 -c 4:collapse -c 5:count_distinct
gloci groupby table.tsv --header -g gene -c expr:median -o medians.tsv
```

### `gloci vcf`

VCF operations (spec §7.8)

```sh
gloci vcf filter cohort.bcf --pass-only --min-qual 30 -o filtered.bcf
gloci vcf filter input.vcf --samples s1,s2 --min-dp 10 --recalc-ac -o out.vcf
gloci vcf filter variants.bcf --types indel --biallelic
```

#### `gloci vcf filter`

Filter VCF/BCF files with the selection pipeline

```sh
gloci vcf filter cohort.bcf --pass-only --min-qual 30 --min-maf 0.01 --max-missing 0.1 -o filtered.bcf
gloci vcf filter input.vcf --samples s1,s2 --min-dp 10 --recalc-ac -o out.vcf
gloci vcf filter variants.bcf --types indel --biallelic
```

#### `gloci vcf extract`

Extract INFO or FORMAT values as a table, or the 012 genotype matrix

```sh
gloci vcf extract cohort.vcf.gz --info DP,AF -o info.tsv
gloci vcf extract cohort.bcf --format GT,DP --layout long --samples s1,s2
gloci vcf extract cohort.vcf.gz --genotype-matrix 012 --out-prefix cohort --biallelic
```

#### `gloci vcf stats`

Compute statistics in one pass: per-site, per-sample and whole-file, written as PREFIX.<ext> in vcftools' formats, plus a summary

```sh
gloci vcf stats cohort.vcf.gz --out-prefix qc --freq --missing-indv --het --summary
gloci vcf stats cohort.bcf --out-prefix qc --depth --site-mean-depth --min-dp 8 --samples s1,s2
gloci vcf stats cohort.vcf.gz --out-prefix qc --tstv-summary --json --pass-only
```

## Migration tables

Every row below was checked against `gloci <cmd> --help`.

### Sorting, indexing and viewing (htslib, bcftools, bedops, bedtools)

| Old command | gloci |
|---|---|
| `sort-bed FILE`, `bedtools sort -i FILE`, `LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1 -k2,2n FILE` | `gloci sort FILE --chrom-order lex` (drop `--chrom-order lex` to get karyotype order) |
| `bedtools sort -i FILE -g GENOME` | `gloci sort FILE -g GENOME` (`-g` also takes a built-in such as `hg38`) |
| `vcf-sort FILE`, `bcftools sort FILE` | `gloci sort FILE` (the order comes from the `##contig` lines; `-g` overrides) |
| `sort-bed --max-mem 8G --tmpdir DIR FILE` | `gloci sort FILE --max-mem 8G --tmp-dir DIR` |
| `sort-bed --check-sort FILE` | `gloci sort --check FILE` (checks chromosome and start, which is what the streaming commands need) |
| `bedops -u A B`, `sort -m A B` | `gloci sort -m A B` (inputs must already be sorted in the same order) |
| `sort-bed FILE \| uniq`, `sort -u` | `gloci sort --unique FILE` (`--duplicates` is `uniq -d`) |
| `bgzip -c FILE > FILE.gz` | `gloci view FILE -o FILE.gz` (always BGZF; `--compression-level N`, `-t` threads) |
| `bgzip -dc FILE.gz > FILE` | `gloci view FILE.gz -o FILE` (the name needs a known extension such as `x.bed`; otherwise add `-O bed`) |
| `tabix -p bed\|vcf\|gff FILE.gz`, `tabix -C ...` | `gloci index FILE.gz` (the type comes from the content; TBI, or CSI when a record ends past 2^29) |
| `tabix -s S -b B [-e E] [-0] [-S N] [-c C] FILE.gz` | `gloci index FILE.gz -s S -b B [-e E] [--zero-based] [--skip-lines N] [--comment C]` |
| `bcftools index FILE.bcf`, `bcftools index -c\|-t FILE.vcf.gz` | `gloci index FILE.bcf` (a BCF always gets a CSI; `.vcf.gz` gets a TBI, or a CSI when needed) |
| `bgzip FILE && tabix -p vcf FILE.gz` | `gloci sort FILE -o FILE.gz --write-index`, or `gloci view FILE -o FILE.gz --write-index` for a file that is already sorted |
| `tabix FILE.gz REGION...`, `bcftools view -r REGION FILE`, `bcftools view -H -r ...` | `gloci view FILE.gz REGION...` (or `--region REGION`; add `--no-header` for `-H`) |
| `tabix -h FILE.gz REGION`, `tabix -H FILE.gz` | `gloci view FILE.gz REGION` keeps the header; `gloci view --header-only FILE.gz` prints only it |
| `tabix -R TARGETS FILE.gz`, `bcftools view -R TARGETS FILE` | `gloci view FILE.gz --regions-file TARGETS.bed` (0-based BED, like `bedextract`) |
| `bedextract CHR FILE`, `bedextract FILE REGIONS.bed` | `gloci view FILE CHR`, or `gloci view FILE --regions-file REGIONS.bed`; add `--assume-sorted` for the binary search on an uncompressed BED file |
| `bcftools view -Ob FILE.vcf`, `bcftools view -Ov FILE.bcf` | `gloci view FILE.vcf -o FILE.bcf`, `gloci view FILE.bcf -O vcf` |

| `intersect` (no mode flag) | `gloci intersect -a A -b B --mode clip` |

| `merge -d -s -c -o` | `gloci merge FILE... -d/--max-gap N -s --count -c/--column COL:OP` (`--delim`, `--empty`, `--sort`) |

| `sort -i FILE [-g GENOME]` | `gloci sort FILE [-g GENOME]` (`--chrom-order lex` reproduces byte order) |

| `genomecov -i x.bed -g G` (`-bg`, `-bga`, `-d`, `-scale`, `-strand`, `-split`, `-5`, `-3`, `-max`) | `gloci genomecov x.bed -g G [--bedgraph \| --bga \| --per-base] [--scale X] [--strand +\|-] [--split] [--5p \| --3p] [--max-depth N]` (`-g` is required, as in bedtools; the input must be sorted, `--sort` sorts it; `-dz` and `-trackline` have no counterpart; BAM input (`-ibam`) is not available until P3) |

### vcftools

| vcftools | gloci |
|---|---|
| `--vcf` / `--gzvcf` / `--bcf` | `gloci vcf filter FILE` (input format is auto-detected from content; `--format` overrides) |
| `--recode`, `--recode-bcf` | `gloci vcf filter FILE ... -o out.vcf.gz` / `-o out.bcf` (or stdout with `-O vcf` / `-O bcf`) |
| `--recode-INFO-all` | default in `gloci vcf filter` (INFO is kept); prune with `--keep-info KEYS` or `--drop-info KEYS` |
| `--chr` / `--not-chr` / `--from-bp` / `--to-bp` | `--chrom CHROM` / `--exclude-chrom CHROM` / `--region CHR:START-END` |
| `--bed` / `--exclude-bed` | `--regions-file FILE.bed` / `--exclude-regions-file FILE.bed` |
| `--positions` / `--exclude-positions`, `--snp` / `--exclude` | `--positions FILE` / `--exclude-positions FILE`, `--ids FILE` / `--exclude-ids FILE` |
| `--keep-only-indels` / `--remove-indels` | `--types indel` / `--exclude-types indel` (also `snv,mnv,ins,del,sv,ref,other`) |
| `--remove-filtered-all`, `--keep-filtered` / `--remove-filtered` | `--pass-only`, `--keep-filter TAGS` / `--remove-filter TAGS` |
| `--keep-INFO` / `--remove-INFO` | `--require-info FLAG` / `--exclude-info FLAG` |
| `--maf` / `--max-maf` / `--mac` / `--max-mac` / `--min-alleles` / `--max-alleles` / `--minQ` | `--min-maf` / `--max-maf` / `--min-mac` / `--max-mac` / `--min-alleles` / `--max-alleles` / `--min-qual` (plus `--biallelic`) |
| `--min-meanDP` / `--max-meanDP`, `--hwe`, `--thin`, `--phased` | `--min-mean-dp` / `--max-mean-dp`, `--hwe`, `--thin`, `--phased-only` |
| **`--max-missing X`** (X = minimum fraction *called*) | **`--max-missing (1 - X)`** (maximum fraction *missing*; e.g. vcftools `0.9` becomes gloci `0.1`; `--max-missing-count N` bounds missing genotype count). Inverted on purpose; vcftools' meaning is a known trap. |
| `--indv` / `--keep` / `--remove-indv` / `--remove` | `--samples` / `--samples-file` / `--exclude-samples` / `--exclude-samples-file` (add `--recalc-ac` to recompute `INFO/AC`, `AN`, `AF`) |
| `--minGQ` / `--minDP` / `--maxDP`, `--remove-filtered-geno-all` | `--min-gq` / `--min-dp` / `--max-dp`, `--mask-filtered-genotypes` |
| `bcftools view -i EXPR` / `-e EXPR` (subset: FORMAT fields GT, DP, GQ only; see [differences.md#expr-format-fields](differences.md#expr-format-fields)) | `gloci vcf filter FILE --include EXPR` / `--exclude EXPR` |
| `vcf-sort`, `vcf-isec`, `vcf-subset` | `gloci sort`, `gloci intersect --match alleles`, `gloci vcf filter --samples ... --recalc-ac` |
| `--freq` / `--counts` | `gloci vcf stats FILE --out-prefix P --freq` / `--counts` (write `P.frq` / `P.frq.count`, same columns) |
| `--depth` / `--site-depth` / `--site-mean-depth` / `--geno-depth` / `--site-quality` | `--depth` / `--site-depth` / `--site-mean-depth` / `--geno-depth` / `--site-quality` (`P.idepth`, `P.ldepth`, `P.ldepth.mean`, `P.gdepth`, `P.lqual`) |
| `--missing-indv` / `--missing-site` | `--missing-indv` / `--missing-site` (`P.imiss`, `P.lmiss`) |
| `--het` / `--hardy` / `--singletons` | `--het` / `--hardy` / `--singletons` (`P.het`, `P.hwe`, `P.singletons`; the singleton carrier after masking differs, [differences.md#vcf-stats-singletons-masked](differences.md#vcf-stats-singletons-masked)) |
| `--FILTER-summary` / `--TsTv-summary` / `--hist-indel-len` | `--filter-summary` / `--tstv-summary` / `--indel-hist` (`P.FILTER.summary`, `P.TsTv.summary`, `P.indel.hist`; the vcftools spellings are accepted as aliases) |
| `--SNPdensity BIN` | `--snp-density BIN` (`P.snpden`; needs sorted input, [differences.md#vcf-stats-snp-density-unsorted](differences.md#vcf-stats-snp-density-unsorted)) |
| `--minGQ` / `--minDP` / `--maxDP` with a statistic | the same `vcf stats` run takes `--min-gq` / `--min-dp` / `--max-dp` (a `.` DP or GQ is not masked, [differences.md#vcf-stats-mask-missing](differences.md#vcf-stats-mask-missing)) |
| several statistics (vcftools allows one per run), `vcf-stats` | one `gloci vcf stats` run with every flag, plus `--summary` / `--json` for an overview (`P.summary.txt`, `P.summary.json`) |
| `--get-INFO KEY` | `gloci vcf extract FILE --info KEY` (adds an ID column; `.` for missing; [differences.md#vcf-extract-info](differences.md#vcf-extract-info)) |
| `--extract-FORMAT-info KEY` | `gloci vcf extract FILE --format KEY --layout wide` (columns are `SAMPLE:KEY`; `--layout long` gives a row per sample; [differences.md#vcf-extract-format-wide](differences.md#vcf-extract-format-wide)) |
| `--012` (writes `out.012`, `.012.indv`, `.012.pos`) | `gloci vcf extract FILE --genotype-matrix 012 --out-prefix out` (same files; haploid and half-missing reference calls count 0; [differences.md#vcf-extract-012](differences.md#vcf-extract-012)) |
| `vcf-concat` | not yet available (`vcf concat`, P2) |
| `--site-pi`, `--window-pi`, `--TajimaD`, `--weir-fst-pop`, `--*-r2`, `--relatedness*` | not yet available (`vcf popgen`, P3) |
| `--diff*`, `vcf-compare` | not yet available (`vcf compare`, P3) |
| `vcf-merge`, `--plink*`, `--IMPUTE`, `--BEAGLE-*`, `--ldhat*` | not planned |

## Pitfalls

- **`--max-missing` is inverted from vcftools:** In `gloci vcf filter`, `--max-missing FRAC` is the *maximum fraction of missing genotypes* (`--max-missing 0.1` allows at most 10% missing, matching `bcftools view -i 'F_MISSING<=0.1'`). In `vcftools`, `--max-missing 0.9` meant at least 90% called. Translate `vcftools --max-missing X` to `gloci vcf filter --max-missing (1 - X)`.
- **`--vcf-span ref` reproduces bedtools, tabix, and bcftools:** gloci defaults to `--vcf-span allele` (trimmed ALT allele footprints; insertions are zero-length points, deletions exclude the anchor base). Pass `--vcf-span ref` when a pipeline expects `[POS-1, POS-1+len(REF))` spans (and add `--inclusive-points` when matching `tabix` or `bedtools` on edge insertions or zero-length BED records).
- **Use `--chrom-order lex` for old sorted files:** Files sorted by `bedtools sort`, `sort-bed`, or `LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1 -k2,2n` are in lexicographic chromosome order (`chr1, chr10, chr2`), which triggers a sortedness error under gloci's default karyotype order. Pass `--chrom-order lex` to accept byte order directly, `--sort` to re-sort on the fly, or `--unsorted` (on relation commands) to index `-b` in memory.
- **`--mode` has no `-m` short flag (and defaults to `any`):** `gloci intersect` defaults to `--mode any` (unique A records with a hit, like `bedtools intersect -u`), not coordinate clipping (`--mode clip`). Always spell `--mode` in full (`--mode any|none|pairs|clip|count`); `-m` is only `gloci sort -m` for merging pre-sorted files.
